# v0.5.0 — Agent Compliance Release

One canon, one writer, one path form. This release removes every known way the
skill's own documentation caused agents to drift from the spec on long
translation runs — contradictory instructions, unreachable role prompts, and
rules that were loaded once and then forgotten.

## Highlights

- **Workers now actually receive their instructions.** Installed adapters
  referenced role prompts through depth-based parent-relative paths, but agent
  runtimes resolve paths from the project root — so dispatched workers ran on a
  ~170-word wrapper stub instead of their ~1,700-word role prompt, and never
  saw the rules they were being graded against. The build script now normalizes
  every reference to root-relative `core/...`, and each wrapper halts with
  `blocked: missing-role-prompt` instead of improvising if the prompt cannot be
  read.
- **Worker Contract Card.** A compact, non-negotiable rule card the Coordinator
  pastes verbatim at the top of every worker prompt. Long-run compliance decays
  when rules are stated once per session; the card re-anchors role fidelity,
  propose-don't-write, never-guess, formal-data preservation, reveal timing,
  the severity scale, and context-pressure honesty at every single dispatch.
- **One canonical eight-phase workflow.** The entrypoint and the long-document
  workflow previously used two different numbering systems (one of them had no
  Research phase at all), forcing the model to pick a side. Canon everywhere
  now: Intake → Scan → Research → Plan → Translate → Merge → QA → Delivery.

## Fixed

- Fifteen-plus internal contradictions eliminated, including:
  - Four conflicting rules about who writes the Unresolved_Issues_Log. Canon:
    workers return `unresolved_items`; the Coordinator is the log's only
    writer. This also removes a parallel-write race between concurrent
    reviewers.
  - Split severity scales (formatting used high/medium/low; everything else
    critical/major/minor). One scale now: critical / major / minor.
  - Contradictory resume order after interruption. Canon: Chunk_Manifest first
    (status truth), then Context_Plan (constraints), then artifact slices.
  - A context-budget example summing to 105% directly beneath the "must not
    exceed 100%" rule. The policy and every example now sum to exactly 100%.
  - A readiness-gate deadlock that required a Glossary before dispatching the
    researchers whose job is to produce the Glossary. The gate is now
    two-tier: a light research-tier gate for Phase 3, the full eight-artifact
    gate for translation and review dispatch.

## Added

- Three release-gating validator checks:
  - **C18** — rejects parent-escaping `../core/` references in distributed
    instruction files.
  - **C19** — enforces the canonical eight-phase numbering in both canon
    files, so dual numbering cannot regress.
  - **C20** — requires the Worker Contract Card definition and its use by the
    Coordinator prompt.
- Seven new regression tests covering built-adapter path integrity, phase
  canon, contract-card enforcement, and the single-writer rule.
- Tag-triggered release automation: pushing `v*` validates, tests, builds all
  six adapter targets, packages the distribution tarball, and publishes the
  GitHub release with curated notes.

## Changed

- Instruction text deduplicated so every rule has exactly one home: role
  authority and readiness gates in `core/workflows/subagents.md`, chunk-size
  presets in `core/schemas/context-plan.md`, resize triggers and per-chunk
  loading in `core/workflows/context-management.md`. Everything else points
  instead of repeating — less to load, nothing to disagree.
- Adapter entrypoints trimmed to pointers; schema examples and all example
  seed artifacts updated to `skill_version: 0.5.0` with 100% budget
  allocations.

## Upgrade Notes

- Rebuild any installed adapter with
  `python scripts/build_adapters.py --platform <target> --dest <path> --force`
  to pick up the corrected root-relative paths — installs built with earlier
  versions carry broken role-prompt references.
- If you maintain custom dispatch tooling, note the two behavioral contracts
  that tightened: workers must not write the Unresolved_Issues_Log, and every
  worker prompt must begin with the Worker Contract Card.

## Verification

- Python compile checks passed.
- Source validation passed in normal and `--release` modes with 0 findings,
  including the new C18/C19/C20 checks.
- Test suite passed: 25/25 tests.
- Portable, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, and generic build targets
  all passed post-build validation with root-relative core references.
- Two independent model-run consistency audits over the full documentation set
  confirmed no remaining phase-numbering, ownership, severity, resume-order,
  or version-string contradictions.
